_doc: Canonical symbol map: semantic name -> Ravenswatch engine function/global. This is the source of truth (like Minecraft mappings). Ghidra names, the loader C++ header, and the Python SDK constants are all GENERATED from this file via `rsmm symbols gen`. Resolution: `raw` joins to data/function_patterns.json by name for version-resilient (byte-pattern) lookup; `anchor` is an inlined routine reached as parent_pattern + offset; `va` is a base-relative absolute (data globals, which have no code pattern). `status`: ok = pattern/anchor resolvable in the current corpus; va = base-relative only; unverified = documented in an older corpus, not yet re-confirmed against the shipped pattern DB.

symbols.name: Account_GetDisplayName
symbols.note: Platform display name for an account object, written into `out` as an MSVC std::string (32 bytes, SSO under 16 chars). One function per platform key: it branches over the strings `gamertag` (Xbox), `personaName` (Steam), `pseudo`, and `Nickname`, so it is the engine's single name abstraction. Its only direct caller is FUN_14044a050, the login/session bring-up, which means this is confirmed for the LOCAL account and not yet proven reachable per-peer. Recorded because the ally-name hunt kept re-deriving it: the exe imports EOSSDK-Win64-Shipping.dll (Lobby/P2P/Connect) and NOT steam_api64.dll, and imports no EOS_UserInfo_* at all, so no ally name can come from the platform SDK - remote names must arrive over the game's own session layer. That they exist at all is settled by the shipped text keys Menu_PauseAskerName and Session_Peer_Disconnect. NOT called by the SDK: it takes an out-string the caller owns and an account pointer we cannot yet validate.

symbols.name: AnalyticsBag_SetInt
symbols.signature: void*(void* bag, void* keyDesc, uint64_t value, void* alloc)
symbols.note: Append an INTEGER property to an analytics bag. Writes the value into slot 2 and a tag of 0x01d6 (plus a sign bit at 53) into slot 3, which is what distinguishes it from the 0x0405 string tag. See AnalyticsBag_SetString for the full layout.

symbols.name: AnalyticsBag_SetString
symbols.signature: void*(void* bag, void* keyDesc, void* valueDesc, void* alloc)
symbols.note:
Append a STRING property to an analytics bag.

BAG LAYOUT, recovered from this function and its integer sibling — this is what the loader's firehose decode is built on:
  bag   +0x00 u32 count, +0x04 u32 capacity, +0x08 u64 data (low 48 bits)
  entry 0x20 bytes: [0] key length, [1] key pointer | tag,
                    [2] value (LENGTH for a string, the integer otherwise),
                    [3] value pointer | tag, or a bare tag for an integer
The TYPE is the top 16 bits of slot 3: 0x0405 means slot 3 holds a string pointer in its low 48 bits; anything else means the value is the integer already in slot 2. Growth is 1.5x from an initial 16 entries.

symbols.name: Analytics_EmitSkillSelected
symbols.signature: void(void* analyticsCtx, float* skillEvent, void* unused)
symbols.note:
Analytics emitter for a TALENT/SKILL selection. Builds a property bag and calls Analytics_SubmitNamedEvent with the event name "skill_selected".

⚠ THIS IS THE TALENT IDENTITY THAT THE GAMEPLAY BUS DOES NOT CARRY, and it corrects a conclusion recorded earlier the same day. A re-mine of the event payload classes proved that UPGRADE_LOWER_SKILL and its siblings are dispatched as the bare oCGameNamedEvent base class, so an R.on subscriber learns THAT a talent was upgraded and never WHICH. That is true, and it was written up as 'talents are a dead end on the event bus, permanently'. The conclusion was too broad: it holds for the gameplay bus only. The ANALYTICS bus carries the name, the tier and the rarity, and the loader already hooks Analytics_SubmitNamedEvent.

FIELDS, read off the emitter:
  skill_tier    (int)  = (int)param_2[0]
  skill_name    (str)  = *(char**)(*(void**)(param_2+0x10) + 0x20)
  skill_rarity  (str)  = *(char**)(*(void**)(param_2+0x10) + 0x38)
  skill_count   (int)  = atoi(*(char**)(*(void**)(param_2+0x10) + 0x50))
So param_2+0x10 holds the SKILL DEFINITION pointer, and that definition keeps its name at +0x20, rarity at +0x38 and a count string at +0x50. Those three offsets are the useful part: anything holding a skill def can be read the same way.

SIBLINGS, same shape, confirmed by their event-name literals:
  FUN_1401f7120  "skill_proposed"  — what the game OFFERED
  FUN_1401f7e50  "unlock_skill"
Together those give offered-vs-taken, which is what a 'build around your POWER ability' or 'first pick defines the build' rule needs.

Found 2026-09-11 only after the exception table was used to define the 16,945 functions Ghidra's heuristics had never created: string search for 'Skill' had previously returned nothing because the binary is stripped and the analysis was 26% short.

symbols.name: Analytics_SubmitNamedEvent
symbols.signature: void(void* analytics_mgr, void* payload_kv, StringDesc* event_name, char has_run_ctx)
symbols.note:
CENTRAL TELEMETRY SINK. ~37 gameplay callers funnel named analytics events through here (run_end, enemy_killed, matchmaking_start, level_up_reach, level_up_book, ...), each building a key-value payload then submitting as JSON (projectId 'passtech-ravenswatch') to Passtech's analytics backend over an authenticated HTTP POST. param_3 is a StringDesc { const char* ptr @+0x0; uint32 len|0x80000000 @+0x8 } holding the event name. The loader 'firehose' detour (hook_events.cpp::install_analytics_firehose) reads that name and re-publishes it to the Lua bus by its raw name, so ONE hook exposes every named event to mods (R.on('enemy_killed', cb)) and survives the game adding new event names. OBSERVATION-GRADE: these fire AFTER the gameplay action and carry analytics KV, not live entity handles — good for 'when X happens do Y' triggers, not for mutating the actor. For entity-context gameplay events (damage, give-item) see the oCGameNamedEvent bus — mapped: NamedEvent_Dispatch is the single hook point (R.on('gameplay:<NAME>'), docs/_re/kinds/events-bus.md). Skips 'run_end' to avoid double-firing the typed Event_RunEnd table hook. [2026-07-10: recovered via anchor/decompile-verify (batch 2) after the July-9 remap mis-placed it.]

[2026-09-11] THE FULL EMITTER CATALOG — 33 call sites, each with its event name and its property names, recovered by scanning every call to this function and reading the string literals in the calling function.

WHY THIS IS THE IMPORTANT ONE. The gameplay bus (oCGameNamedEvent) tells a mod that something happened; the ANALYTICS bus tells it WHAT. Most of the identity questions this project has treated as unreachable are answered here as plain strings — which item was offered and taken, which talent, which shop article and for how much, which enemy killed you. The mod-side consequence is large: mods/saga currently leaves 40 challenge rules on the honour system, and a majority of them are about exactly these facts.

Two specific plans this OBSOLETES:
  * the magical-object GUID join. `object_selected` carries object_name as a STRING, so there is no need to map a 128-bit GUID from the give event back to a corpus entry, and no playtest needed to discover which GUID the event carries.
  * 'talent identity is unobtainable'. See Analytics_EmitSkillSelected.

symbols.name: BinarySaver_CollectDependencies
symbols.note: The pre-pass that makes Object_SaveToFile self-contained, NOT a gate (it is the `if (FUN_1404fc950() == 1)` at the head of BinarySaver_WriteGraph). It builds an `oCDependencyParser` — another oISerializer implementation — over the saver's own class table (saver+0x18 +0x6d0/+0x6d8) and object list (+0x6e0/+0x6e8), then calls rootObject->vtbl[3](rootObject, parser) = Serialize. Walking the graph through a fake serializer is how the file's class directory and sub-object list get populated: the caller supplies ONE root object and the engine discovers the rest, versions included. It then drains the collected list, serializing each into the parser, and returns false if any object's Serialize fails.

symbols.name: BinarySaver_WriteGraph
symbols.signature: bool(void* saver, void* rootObject, const char* label, void* ctx)
symbols.note: oCBinarySaver vtable slot 5 (the loader's slot 5 is FUN_140500d70, the reader). Writes the whole cooked file body: `uClassCount`, then per class {rInfo.m_sName, m_uId, m_uVersionMaj, m_uVersionMin, m_uParentId} (0x20 bytes/record, table at saver+0x18 +0x6d0/+0x6d8), then `uOjbectsCount` (engine's typo), then per object its class-table index as `uFoundIndex`, then each sub-object as `SingleObject%d`, then the root. This is byte-for-byte the header rsmm.engine.cooked.parse reads back, INCLUDING the per-class version fields Serializer_GetClassVersion gates optional fields on.

symbols.name: BinarySaver_WriteObject
symbols.signature: bool(void* saver, void* object, const char* label, bool flag)
symbols.note: Writes ONE object through a serializer: calls object->vtbl[1]() = GetClassId, finds that id in the saver's class table, writes the index as `uFoundIndex`, then calls object->vtbl[3](object, saver) = Serialize. PROOF that Serialize is direction-agnostic: slot 3 is the same slot the codec work calls 'Deserialize' (e.g. GameModeDefaultDefinition::Deserialize = vftable slot 3). A def's Serialize branches on serializer vtable slot 4 = IsSaving (oCBinaryLoader returns 0, oCBinarySaver returns 1) -- Definition_DeserializeBase does exactly this at its head -- and transfers fields via the typed slots 13-19 (widths 1/4/8), which read from the loader's stream at +0x68 or write to the saver's at +0x40. So every hand-written Serialize in the engine can WRITE the payloads rsmm's Python codecs still carry as opaque _tail_hex.

symbols.name: Component_GetTypeId
symbols.note:
Component TYPE ID — vftable slot 1 on the Controller family. The body is a single `return <imm32>`: each component class returns its own constant id. 36 implementations, none named before this.

CONFIRMED AGAINST AN INDEPENDENT SOURCE. tools/mine_class_ids.py, which resolves 1546 registered classes straight from the exe, maps the two constants read here exactly: 0x18e07849 -> oCDtEntityCpntMinimapUiController and 0x15c57095 -> oCDtEntityCpntMainMenuUiController. So slot 1 returns the SAME id space the class registry uses, reached by a completely different route (vtable slot vs registry walk).

WHY IT IS USEFUL AT RUNTIME. It gives a live 'what is this component?' oracle. Given any component pointer, read its vftable slot 1 to get the id, then hand that id to mine_class_ids for the class NAME. That is the honest way to identify a component a mod has stumbled on, and the alternative to the offset-guessing this project has repeatedly had to disprove — see Entity_GetComponentByTester, which finds a component by asking each one's class rather than by a fixed slot.

⚠ The 'Controller' family as the miner groups it is name-suffix based, so it also sweeps in Bullet physics classes (btKinematicCharacterController). Those are NOT part of this interface — their slot 1 is an ordinary virtual call, not a constant return. Check the body shape before trusting family membership.

symbols.name: Controller_GetFieldByKey
symbols.note:
KEYED FIELD ACCESSOR on the Controller family — `void* (this, u32 key)`, returning a pointer to one of the controller's own members, or null when the key is unknown. The body is a flat chain of integer compares, one per exposed field.

NOT ONE SLOT BUT A BANK OF THEM. Slots 11, 12, 13, 15 and 17 all have this identical shape (22, 15, 14, 4 and 15 implementations), which reads as one accessor per data CATEGORY rather than five unrelated methods. Examples:
  slot 15  oCDtEntityCpntHeroController      5 keys -> +0x1918..+0x19c8
  slot 15  oCDtEntityCpntCharacterController 7 keys -> +0xc8..+0x928
  slot 11  oCDtEntityCpntCinematicUiController 3 keys -> +0x18, +0x38, +0xa8
  slot 17  oCDtEntityCpntMainMenuUiController  1 key  -> +0x138
This is the engine's reflection-style access to component state, and it is the natural read/write surface for a mod that wants a named field on a controller instead of a hardcoded offset.

⚠ THE KEYS CANNOT BE NAMED OFFLINE — a negative result worth keeping, because it is the obvious next thing to attempt. Each key appears EXACTLY ONCE in the whole executable, inside its own accessor: no caller passes a literal, so callers compute the key at runtime. The obvious theory, that a key is a hash of the field's display name, is FALSE. Tested against the 117 known (key, name) pairs recovered from the entity-value registry using FNV-1a-32, FNV-1-32, CRC32, djb2 and sdbm across six casing/spacing variants, with and without a 31-bit mask: ZERO matches.

What they are instead: sequentially ASSIGNED ids. symbols.name: Definition_PreloadResourceCache
symbols.note:
Load a definition's `.UsedRscCache.ot` and hand its contents to the resource system. THIS is the path a definition's transitive dependencies actually arrive by, and it is not ResourceRef_Resolve.

Three steps: FUN_140310ca0(def, <global>); build the cache path with the sibling-name builder (appends ".UsedRscCache.ot" and applies the \\->! collapse, keeping the first two backslashes); parse it with ResourceCache_Parse into a vector of 0x38-byte entries — the same stride as a resource ref block — and pass that vector to ResourceCache_Submit at *(def+0x30)+0x68. Then free the vector, walking it at stride 0x38.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE ADDITIVE-POI WALL. A 2026-09-11 trace on ResourceRef_Resolve, filtered on a mod's own asset names, showed the mod's GEOMETRY and TEXTURES resolving with live objects and state=1 while the mod-added ENTITY produced zero hits — and the filter did include it. So the entity is not merely resolving to null, it is never asked for THROUGH THAT FUNCTION. This preload is the other candidate path, and the two must be told apart before the recorded conclusion ("a mod-added entity resolves to null") can be trusted: it may have been measured with the wrong instrument.

symbols.name: Definition_Unload
symbols.note:
Definition TEARDOWN — vftable slot 19 on the oCDtDefinition family, and the exact inverse of slot 18 (PostLoad). Every implementation does the same three things: release the definition's shared refs and null its resolved resource slots, walk its 0x38-stride ref vectors decrementing each element's refcount, and call Registry_UnregisterInstance(this) — gated, like PostLoad's register, on a vftable predicate. Returns 1.

WHY IT MATTERS. PostLoad is already the hook point content injection uses: once it returns, a definition is fully populated and registered. Slot 19 is where the engine takes it back out. Anything injected at PostLoad is freed here, so it is both the cleanup hook a mod should respect and the first place to look when an injected object outlives its definition — the talent-clone crashes of 2026-09-11 were both inside a destructor walking a definition's ref vectors.

13 implementations, 12 of them unnamed before this. Found by tools/mine_vtable_interfaces.py, which reports 82 such interface slots with three or more implementations — a figure that is only meaningful now that the Ghidra project has every .pdata entry point defined as a function (it was 74% before 2026-09-11, so slot targets in the missing quarter were invisible to the miner).

symbols.name: Entity_GetNetComponent
symbols.note: SwissTable/F14 component-map lookup on an entity for the fixed type-id 0x154fce5c (the net/replication component). Probes the entity's component map (control bytes @entity+0x5e8, slots @entity+0x5f0, bucket mask @entity+0x600) and returns the component pointer, or 0 if the entity has none (e.g. single-player / non-replicated). The returned component's byte @+0x130 is the local/remote AUTHORITY flag: 0 = locally controlled (this client owns the entity and emits its NETWORK_DAMAGE), nonzero = remotely controlled (apply received state, don't emit). Both hit paths (NamedEvent_EmitNetworkDamageFromHit, the attack resolver FUN_1403dc780) gate network emit on this flag. NOTE: it dereferences the component map unconditionally, so only call on a known-valid entity. Pattern is multi-match (index 3/6, 128-byte sig) — fn_verify-guarded. Relevant to local-vs-remote hero disambiguation in co-op, though hero-capture already pins the local player via the HUD-mirror requirement (only the local player has one). That makes the map walkable LINEARLY with page-guarded reads and no hash function, which is how R.damage classifies a damage victim (enemy = carries class id 0x1561073c). The id space is mined by tools/mine_class_ids.py; 0x154fce5c resolving to oCEntityCpntNetwork is that miner's acceptance test. NO FIXED COMPONENT SLOTS: because the map is a hash table, an entity component is NOT reachable at any constant offset from the entity, so a chain of the form `entity+CONST -> +CONST` can never be a structural path to a component (or to anything a component owns). The only qword-pointer write at +0x678 in entity-shaped code is oe::dt::EntityCpntRecapBookPageSettings::~dtor (FUN_140419aa0), an unrelated UI class. Both chains were heap coincidence; they are no longer seeded, and a chain is only used once observed on the live board. Do not re-derive per-player identity as a constant entity offset.

symbols.note: ⚠ MISNAMED — SETTLED 2026-09-18 by static RE: this modifies the hero's DREAM SHARDS, not HP. Evidence: (1) the gained/lost events it fires are 0x12e831f3/0x12e831f4 = dt_shard_gain/dt_shard_loss (gamevalues.lua); (2) it clamps only at 0 (maxss with 0), never to a maximum; (3) gains accumulate into mirror+0x10 and 'Purchase'-tagged spends into mirror+0x4 (lifetime earned/spent totals); (4) the Sandman buy routine 0x140370f10 checks [ctrl+0xc8]+0x15c8 >= price then calls this with -price and tags {Sandman, Purchase}; (5) hero capture always landed within 0.2 s of GAIN_DREAM_SHARDS and +0x15c8 reads 0 at run start. So +0x15c8 = current dream shards; +0x15cc/+0x15d4 feed a ratio at +0x15d0 and are NOT max HP. R.combat.heal/damage/set_hp and R.entity.hp/max_hp/hp_frac therefore read/write shards. Earlier text below is kept for history and is WRONG about HP. — Core HP-modification routine on the hero CHARACTER object (delta>0 heals, delta<0 damages) — the engine's own heal/damage primitive, with clamping, the UI mirror write, analytics submit, and the gained/lost named-event cascade. IMPORTANT: hero is NOT the bus dispatcher and NOT dispatcher-0x4d8 (that was a wrong guess that crashed; the dispatcher and the hero character are separate heap objects). The hero is baked into each event subscription as the handler's param_1 — capture it by hooking a hero-bound handler (Entity_GainHealthHandler / Entity_GiveHandler, both param_1=hero, pointer-only sigs). HERO HEALTH LAYOUT: current HP f32 @hero+0x15c8, max HP f32 @hero+0x15cc, missing-health ratio @+0x15d0, UI/display mirror pointer @hero+0x1d80 (the routine writes new HP to both +0x15c8 and *(*(hero+0x1d80))). HERO-ONLY — DO NOT call on enemies: param_1+0x1d80 (the HUD mirror) is dereferenced UNCONDITIONALLY for any nonzero delta (`**(param_1+0x1d80)=newHP`, plus `*(*(param_1+0x1d80)+0x10)` on heal and a +0x1db0 secondary mirror) — an enemy/non-player entity has no HUD mirror there, so calling this on one access-violates. Enemy damage must use a different path (the hit-data network-damage event NamedEvent_EmitNetworkDamageFromHit / oCGameNamedEventNetworkDamage, which carries a full oCEntityHitData), NOT this routine. R.combat is therefore correctly hero-scoped. sourceTags = an oCCustomFlagList ctx (vftable @va 0x140efc320, then {list=0, count=0}); an EMPTY flag list {vftable,0,0} is accepted. Verified by decompiling the inbound GAIN_HEALTH handler FUN_1403993f0, which calls this twice: damage = ModifyHealth(hero, -amt, tags{'Damage'}), heal = ModifyHealth(hero, +amt, tags). Exposed via R.entity / R.combat in rsmm.lua. Float arg requires the (ptr,float,ptr) prototype added to fn_call.cpp. [2026-07-09 patch: prologue changed, not re-confirmed; needs manual RE.] [2026-07-09: recovered — (hero,float) sig, heal/damage sign-branch, hero+0x1d80 carrier, decompile-verified.]

Proof: the sole caller FUN_1403c7560 passes its own param_2 to Entity_GetNetComponent (FUN_140312db0) and touches it at +0x28 / +0x4d8, i.e. an oCEntity; inside this function param_2+0x28 is the entity's definition object, whose +0x70 resource path is stringified into the analytics record (falling back to "Unknown") and whose flag lists at +0x2c0 / +0x318 are appended to it. symbols.name: HeroStats_OnDamageTaken
symbols.note:
Per-hero damage-taken accounting; the counterpart to HeroStats_OnDamageDealt and the source of the meter's `taken` column. Found from the stat id 0x17df7da0 referenced at 0x1403a0c8d, with the function bounds taken from .pdata because Ghidra had no function defined there. param_2 carries the amount at +0x10 (the same value is mirrored at +0xa0). Unlike the dealt hook this is NOT a session-wide feed: a hit on an ally is applied on the ALLY's machine, so a remote player's taken is always 0 here. That is netcode, not a bug - the mod documents it. Hook shape 'vpp'.

[2026-09-11] DECOMPILED for the first time — the address was never a Ghidra function until the exception table was used to define the 16,945 functions its heuristics had missed.

What it does: resolves the GAME EVENT scene context (a different tester from the global entity-value one — oCGameEventSceneContext), builds an oCCustomFlagList naming the damage source, and emits it under the entity-value keys 0x17df7da0 ("Damage dealt") and, when the hit flag at +0x11 is set, 0x17fdac33 ("Damage received").

LAYOUT worth keeping: the attacker name falls back to the literal "Unknown" when the source chain is absent, which is the engine's own answer to the ally-naming problem R.damage spent sessions on. A per-hit log is appended at hero+0x1758 (data), +0x1760 (count), +0x1764 (cap), stride 0xc, and the running total is accumulated into the HUD mirror at *(hero+0x1d80)+0xc. WHY IT MATTERS: player display names cannot come from the platform SDK (the exe imports EOSSDK-Win64-Shipping.dll and no EOS_UserInfo_*; Steam can name only the local account), so a remote name reaches this machine ONLY as a lobby attribute. Detouring this is how R.lobby learns names without sweeping the address space: the 32-byte key/value blocks the old scan searched for are this parse's TRANSIENT storage, not a persistent roster, which is why a 4-player session scanned back only 2 members.

symbols.name: SkillController_SetTier
symbols.note:
Sets a talent's tier (rarity) and switches on that tier's state. ⚠ NOT A GRANT BY ITSELF — PROVEN IN-GAME 2026-09-12: every controller, owned or not, already carries a tier (the level-up offer builder FUN_1403a9cb0 stamps one on each card), and calling this on an unowned talent changed nothing. Ownership is the held slot; see HeroController_AddSkill. ADD_ALL_SKILLS (handler FUN_1402eef80) is this call followed by EntityComponent_Activate(*(ctrl+0x80)), which enters the talent's state; it still does not fill held slots.

Body: **(ctrl+0x68) = tier; if ctrl sits in the hero's 10 held-skill slots (heroCtrl+0xff0, stride 0x20, heroCtrl = ctrl+0x78) it refreshes the replicated HUD copy at *(heroCtrl+0x1db0); then FUN_1402eef10(ctrl, tier), which resets ctrl+0x108 and turns on exactly ONE of four tier states at +0x128/+0x148/+0x168/+0x188 (tier 0..3 = Common..Legendary). Pick/upgrade paths follow it with FUN_140203b20(ctrl+0x1c0, ctrl) and FUN_140713b00(ctrl+0x1e8).

It does NOT insert the controller into the held slots, so the HUD talent strip may not list a talent granted this way; the effect still runs.

Controller layout (from its activation, FUN_1402ed820): +0x08 owning entity, +0x10 settings (settings+0x178 = category), +0x68 int* tier (4 = special/unowned path), +0x78 hero controller (the object R.entity.hero() captures: HeroSubscribeAll does mov r14,rcx). Every controller registers itself in a per-category {data,u32 count} vector at heroCtrl+0xf98+category*0x10; only category 1 (the normal talent pool) subscribes to ADD_ALL_SKILLS, on entity+0x500.

Found 2026-09-12 by following ADD_ALL_SKILLS: 8 per-file intern globals, one read by FUN_1402ed820; its bound functor thunk 0x140302b50 jumps to FUN_1402eef80. UPGRADE_SPECIFIC_SKILL (handler FUN_1403a79e0) is NOT a grant: it bumps the rarity of an ALREADY-HELD slot chosen by payload index.

symbols.name: HeroController_AddSkill
symbols.note:
Acquires a talent: what taking a level-up card does. Returns at once if ctrl is already held. Otherwise writes ctrl into the first empty of the 10 held slots (hero+0xff0+slot*0x20; the slot's category is at +0xfe0, its UI object at +0xfe8), subscribes the hero to ctrl's tier-change channel (ctrl+0x108/+0x110; node kept at hero+0x1120+slot*8), refreshes the slot UI (FUN_14043cbe0) and the replicated HUD copy at *(hero+0x1db0) (+0x28 id from ctrl+0x62, +0x3c tier from **(ctrl+0x68)), stores the KV 'hero.skill.{slot}' = the talent's name (FUN_140711ff0(settings)), notifies the magical-object component with settings+0x88 (the talent's identity GUID), recounts categories (FUN_1403a9990 / FUN_1403a96c0 / FUN_1403a95d0), and decrements the pending-picks counter hero+0x1374 when non-zero.

Set the tier FIRST (SkillController_SetTier): the HUD copies the tier at add time.

hero is the object R.entity.hero() captures (the same one whose +0xff0 UPGRADE_SPECIFIC_SKILL reads). Inverse: HeroController_RemoveSkill. Found 2026-09-12 by scanning .text for displacements 0xfe0/0xff0 and resolving hits through .pdata.

symbols.name: HeroController_RemoveSkill
symbols.signature: void(HeroController* hero, oCDtEntityCpntSkillController* ctrl, bool clear_hud)
symbols.note: Inverse of HeroController_AddSkill. Finds ctrl in the held slots (returns if absent), clears the HUD copy when clear_hud, erases the 'hero.skill.{slot}' KV, unsubscribes the tier channel, nulls hero+0xff0+slot*0x20, clears the slot UI, recounts. symbols.name: EntityComponent_Activate
symbols.note:
Activates an entity component (refcounted). Returns without effect when cpnt is null, when (*(cpnt+0x08)+0x220) & 4 is set, when FUN_1407274a0(cpnt) or the vfunc at vtable+0xd0 (can-activate) says no. Otherwise either runs the activation (FUN_140712d60) or bumps the activation counter cpnt+0x5e depending on flags at cpnt+0x64. The first argument is not read (callers leave XMM0 garbage in it); pass 0.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR TALENTS: a skill controller's resolved [State] target is at ctrl+0x80, and entering that state is what switches a talent's behaviour on. Both the level-up card confirm (FUN_14039cf80: Activate(*(ctrl+0x80)); HeroController_AddSkill; EntityEventTrigger_Fire(ctrl+0x260)) and the ADD_ALL_SKILLS cheat (FUN_1402eef80: SetTier then `mov rdx,[rsi+0x80]; jmp 0x140712c50`) make this call. A grant that only fills the held slot leaves the state inactive: measured in-game 2026-09-12, damage scaling tied to tier signals applied but the state-gated POWER finisher did not.

symbols.note: REMOVE a subscription from a channel node (the events corpus mislabeled this 'Subscribe' — verified 2026-06-11 it is the unsubscribe). arg1 = channel_node+0x08 (the {array,count|cap,cursor} triple), arg2 = address of the holder's subscription-handle slot. symbols.note: MSVC std::unordered_map<uint64,...>::try_emplace for the netcode's CONNECTION REGISTRY. symbols.name: Netcode_PeerSlots
symbols.signature: PeerSlot[]  // 0x60 stride; live count at Netcode_PeerCount
symbols.note: Global array of connected-peer slots — the engine's own list of the OTHER machines in the run, one slot per remote player, and the only structure that carries a remote player's DISPLAY NAME outside the lobby-attribute path. Mined 2026-08-21 with Ghidra. ⚠ BASE IS 0x14143f600, NOT 0x14143f650. Netcode_PeerStateTick's `lea rax,[rip+...]` lands on 0x14143f650 because it indexes slot+0x50 (the tunnel pointer) directly; reading the array from there is off by 0x50 and every field comes back from the NEXT slot. The true base is what the slot ctor FUN_1402aedf0 zeroes field by field. Stride 0x60 is fixed by `lea rax,[rax+rax*2]; shl rax,5`. SLOT LAYOUT (FUN_1402aedf0 fills it, FUN_1402b5db0 frees it): +0x00 PlayerName, +0x10 the lobby member's own +0x00 session-id string, +0x20 m_sEosUserId (the engine calls it the "P2P User"), +0x30 uint64 hash of the EOS id (FUN_1402aed50), +0x48 connection handle carrying the SystemAddress, +0x50 the P2P tunnel (+0xc0 uint16 UDP port — FUN_1402aa470 passes it through Ordinal_15 = ntohs, so it is a PORT and NOT a RakNet system index; +0xcc conn-state enum, 3 = connected, 2 = eInterrupted; +0xd0 a timestamp). The three string members are the engine's {void* ptr @+0x0; int32 len @+0x8; uint32 cap @+0xc} descriptor, the same shape LobbyAttributes_Parse's StringDesc uses. HOW THE FIELDS WERE PROVEN: FUN_1402aedf0 calls FUN_140918b00(session_mgr, param_1, &record), which walks the lobby members (0x70 stride), memcmp's each member's +0x00 string against param_1, and on a match runs LobbyAttributes_Parse(&record, member+0x28) — so param_1, stored at slot+0x10, IS the member session id, and the record fields copied out to slot+0x00 and slot+0x20 are record+0x00 (PlayerName) and record+0xa8 (m_sEosUserId) by their stack offsets. FUN_1402b0230 finds the LOCAL slot by comparing slot+0x10 to the global at 0x141300958; FUN_1402b0170 finds a slot by slot+0x20. FUN_140272700 is the engine's own member->slot join: it hashes each parsed member's EOS id and compares against slot+0x30, logging "No tunnel found for P2P User: {}" / "No party member found for P2P User: {}" with slot+0x20 as the argument. WHY IT WAS MINED: the damage board knows every player NAME and a distinct per-row owner RakNetGUID (Entity_GetNetId's note) and nothing joined the two. This table supplies the name directly; the open half is which slot owns which hero row, and slot+0x30 is the engine's own ownership key, so rsmm.lua's F._dmg_peer_join scans each row's controller and entity for it. UNPROVEN in-game. ⚠ va, so build-specific: gate every read on va_globals_trusted. [IN-GAME 2026-08-21, session a34f] The layout READS BACK CORRECTLY on live data: `peer table: 2 peer(s) [#0 fruktik_kiwi eos=0002742cd3f241e6821afcd414945c85 port=59550 state=3, #1 EvilMurray eos=0002b4fab7154a739ef4154809c7f6ea port=33421 state=3]` — real personas at +0x00, real ProductUserIds at +0x20, live ports and state=3 through the tunnel at +0x50, and the peer count equalled the number of remote machines. So this IS a working name table for remote players. ⚠ TWO NEGATIVES from the same session. (1) slot+0x30 is NOT a hash value: it reads 0x2a114260 / 0x2bfbe3a0, i.e. heap addresses in the game's own allocation range, so FUN_1402aed50 returns a POINTER (probably to the interned id) and comparing it across processes is meaningless. (2) Nothing on the hero side carries it: scanning 0x800 of every row's controller and entity gave `hash hits [none]`, and the netcomp locator sweep found +0x2d0/+0x2e8/+0x300 pointing at the SAME player's id on EVERY row — a shared object, not a per-player field. The hero->peer link is therefore NOT on the hero object. The only per-row distinct value remains RakNet::Replica3::creatingSystemGUID, so the next candidate is GUID -> SystemAddress -> the tunnel's +0xc0 PORT, which this table already exposes.

Reads a vector of polymorphic sub-object pointers: u32 count (0xaabb1111 sentinel = optional inline class-header {lstr name, u32 x2} first — not hit in cooked files, where sub-objects live in their own sections referenced by u32 sub-object id), then per element reader-vtbl+0xa8 poly resolve. Count clamped to 1,000,000. Write path labels 'Vector.Length' / 'Vector[%d]'. Vec layout {data @+0x0, u32 size @+0x8, u32 cap @+0xc}. [2026-07-09 patch: prologue changed, not re-confirmed; needs manual RE.] [2026-07-09: recovered via hash/decompile verification.]

[2026-09-11] WHY THE SKILL-VECTOR COUNT WAS NEVER FOUND, and why the net-new-talent wall should be re-opened. The binary path reads a u32 and, if it equals the 0xaabb1111 MARK, consumes a class-name string plus two u32s (and optionally a second such block) BEFORE reading the real count. The count is therefore NOT at a fixed distance ahead of the rows, which is exactly why docs/_re/kinds/skills-system.md concluded 'there is no plain u32==28 count anywhere in the .gen before the rows (scanned all heroes)' and attributed the failure to 'a count living in the registrar region Ghidra leaves unanalysed'. The count is in the stream; the scan was looking in the wrong place.

The engine then allocates exactly `count` pointer slots and loops exactly `count` times, rejecting anything above 1,000,000. So a spliced skill row is an ORPHAN in precisely the sense CLAUDE.md already documents for entities (fixed 2026-09-06) and levels (fixed 2026-09-08): the bytes are in the stream and the vector that owns them was not grown. The Aladdin 'whole hero fails to load' result is consistent with that and does not require a hidden registrar format.

[2026-09-12] The element reader at reader-vtbl+0xa8 is now read, not inferred: Serializer_ResolveObjectId. An element id is an index into the object table that Serializer_ReadObjectNamed builds from `uOjbectsCount`, with 0xffffffff = null and 0xfffffffe = the root. So growing one of these vectors is only half an append — the id it adds has to BE an object, which means `uOjbectsCount` and its `uClassFinfoIndex` list have to grow too. rsmm.engine.entity_append does both (`_directory` + `component_vector`, asserted by `validate_layout`); rsmm.engine.level_placements.add_placement does only the vector.

symbols.name: TileDef_Deserialize
symbols.note:
Tile definition deserializer — vftable slot 3 on oCDtTileDefinition (vftable 0x140ed6048, found via RTTI type descriptor -> complete object locator). Calls Definition_DeserializeBase first and bails on failure, the same shape as the rest of the oCDtDefinition family.

⚠ ALMOST EVERY FIELD IS VERSION-GATED, AND THE SHIPPED VERSION IS 1. Each optional block is guarded by `FUN_1404fce50(stream, out, 0x1781ca4d)` followed by a compare on the returned `+0x4`, which is the SCHEMA VERSION for class uid 0x1781ca4d. The gates read `< 2`, `< 3`, `< 5`, `< 6`, `< 7` and `< 8`, and each one SKIPS its block when the version is below the threshold.

The three tier/slot counts live behind the LAST of those:
    if (version >= 8) {
        read(&this->field_0x2fc);   // tier 1
        read(&this->field_0x300);   // tier 2
        read(&this->field_0x304);   // tier 3
    }

MEASURED IN THE CORPUS: the uid appears once per tiledef at file offset 0x35, immediately followed by the version — and it reads **1** in both a shipped tile (6x6_Bleeding_01) and a mod clone. Version 1 is below every gate, so on this build NONE of those optional fields is deserialized, the tier counts included.

WHY THAT MATTERS: it kills a plausible-looking hypothesis. A playtest showed mod tiles reading 0/0/0 for the tier fields while two shipped tiles read non-zero, which looks exactly like "our tiles ship a weight nobody set". They do not — nobody's tiledef authors those fields on this build, because the deserializer never reaches them. Whatever gives a shipped tile a non-zero tier weight is assigned at RUNTIME from another source, and looking for it in the cooked file is a dead end.

symbols.name: UiButton_PressCommit
symbols.note: RE-UNDERSTOOD 2026-07-19: there is NO click-only choke-point function on this build -- the old FUN_14069f8e0 was inlined away. symbols.name: g_GlobalEntityValueSceneContext_Tester_vftable
symbols.note:
Vftable of oCTKindOfTypeTester<oCGlobalEntityValueSceneContext, oIGameSceneContext>, read from MSVC RTTI (the complete object locator one qword before the vftable names the class exactly). This is the ONE missing piece between the loader and roughly a hundred engine-authored gameplay values.

THE RECIPE, read off the reroll-counter writer at 0x1403aaa0d..0x1403aaa4f and not guessed:
  1. Stack-construct the tester: two `lea` writes to the SAME slot, the second (this vftable) overwriting the first (oITTester<oIGameSceneContext>, 0x140f11fd8) -- ctor then vftable fixup, so the SECOND is the live one. Taking the first is the obvious mistake here, and it yields a tester that matches nothing and returns null.
  2. ctx = GameScene_FindContextByTester(gameScene, &tester)  [status=ok, pattern-resolved]
  3. EntityValue_Get(ctx, &out, crcKey)                       [status=ok, pattern-resolved]
Both functions already resolve today; only this VA is build-specific, so a capability built on it must gate on va_globals_trusted the way the event payload decode does.

WHAT IT UNLOCKS -- 117 named values harvested from the four registration routines (EntityValueRegistry_RegisterAll plus three siblings, 177 call sites). These are the ENGINE's own answers to questions mods currently infer. Highlights: 'Is in sandman shop' (every shop rule), 'Reroll count' (every no-reroll rule), 'Current chapter' (hand-counted today), 'Is in overtime' and 'Is boss awaken', 'Active Enemies Count' (a real in-combat signal instead of a boss/tumor proxy), 'Is Session Host', 'Revive token', 'Current dream shards count'.

NOTE ON is_in_main_menu: the loader currently answers this by sniffing which cooked file was opened in the last 5 seconds (Loader::is_in_main_menu, the HgdzHqzw prefix heuristic). Key 0x181d17fe IS 'Is in main menu' in the Player location family, so that heuristic has an exact replacement once this context is reachable.

HARVEST METHOD, because the naive version is confidently wrong: a registration is a `mov ecx, <key>` plus three string pointers passed through frame slots, and the string register is hoisted OUT of the call block in most cases. Pairing a key with the nearest `lea`, forwards or backwards, produces a table shifted by one entry that looks entirely plausible. Follow the argument set-up instead -- `lea reg,[rip+s]`, then `mov [rbp+N],reg`, then `lea r8,[rbp+N]` -- so r8 is the display name and r9 the category. The self-check is that every row in a family carries the SAME category string, and that consecutive names take consecutive keys.

symbols.name: TileSpawn_PlaceTiles
symbols.note: The map-generation driver, 0x1543 bytes, sole caller TileSpawner_Spawn (slot 7) at 0x1403436e9, same `this`. Calls TileSpawn_DistanceConstraints (the min/max-distance solver) and GameScene_FindContextByTester x5. This is where a tile is CHOSEN for a slot, so it is the function to read when working out where the chosen set is stored — but it is NOT the hook point: it is mid-generation, and the useful moment is after its caller returns. Prefer detouring TileSpawner_Spawn. ★ PLACEMENT OUTPUT LAYOUT, recovered 2026-09-04 by reading the post-placement pass at 0x140345410 (the call right after this one in slot 7), which walks what this function wrote. Four members on the spawner, all written here and read there: +0x110 = array of {void* data, u32 count} groups (stride 0x10), +0x118 = number of groups, +0x120/+0x128 = a flat vector of the same element type. ELEMENTS ARE 0x58 BYTES and the engine SKIPS any whose +0x10 is null (`cmp qword [rbx+0x10], 0` at 0x140345460), so +0x10 is the payload pointer and a null there is an unused slot, not a bad read; live elements are passed to FUN_1403429d0 with spawner+0x80 as arg 2. ⚠ DO NOT look for this with R.debug.find_arrays: that scans the data@+0x190 convention, and on this object every hit it returns is the scene QUADTREE (oCBasicQuadTree2Agent / oCBasicQuadTree2 / oCTerrainSubLayerOutput) -- confirmed in-game across three launches, with the populated count varying by map, which reads convincingly like placement data and is not. R.poi.describe reads these offsets instead. MEASURED IN-GAME 2026-09-04 (session 3036, Dark Hills): 4 groups of 62 / 57 / 14 / 5 elements plus a 5-slot flat list (4 empty), and EVERY live payload at +0x10 is an `oCEntitySettingsResource` -- 138 of them. So the placement output is a per-group list of entity-settings resources, which is the tile-instance side rather than the definition side. RTTI names the type and the type is identical for all of them, so it does NOT identify which tile; the resource's own PATH string does, and R.poi.describe samples it via R.interact.identify. ★★ SOLVED IN-GAME 2026-09-04 (session 0936). The payload's resource NAME is a char* at payload+0xa0 — 139/139 read cleanly, zero misses, so the offset is confirmed rather than inferred. The four groups are TILE FOOTPRINT CLASSES: group 0 = 3x3 (62), 1 = 6x6 (57), 2 = 40x40 (14), 3 = 64x64 (5), plus a 5-slot flat list that is mostly empty. Counts stay identical across different generated maps while the NAMES change — a fixed slot topology filled with varying tiles — and group 2 holds 14 of the 34 pooled 40x40 tiles, i.e. a SELECTION, which is what makes this the placed set and not the pool. ⚠ Names are SANITISED: a mod tile from id `additive-poi-test` appears as `additive_poi_test_camp_swap`. Matching a manifest id verbatim scored 0 of 139 against a list that visibly contained the tile — a false negative shaped exactly like the real failure. Normalise punctuation on both sides. R.poi.placed() returns (names, misses). ★★★ THE LIST IS THE BUILT SET, NOT A SELECTION — settled by RE 2026-09-04, no sighting needed. The post-placement pass calls FUN_1403429d0(element, spawner+0x80) per live element (0x81d bytes); that function WRITES element+0x18 with a spawned ENTITY and manages the back-link properly: if the old +0x18 was non-null it detaches via FUN_1406f78f0(old+0x570, &elem[0x18]), stores the new entity (`mov [r12+0x18], rbx` @0x140342f02), then attaches via FUN_1406f79b0(new+0x570, ..., &elem[0x18]). entity+0x570 is the engine's weak-reference back-link vector, named independently elsewhere in this map. A candidate or pool list does not own an entity handle and does not register a death-watch on it. ELEMENT LAYOUT so far: +0x08 ptr, +0x10 settings resource (name at resource+0xa0), +0x18 SPAWNED ENTITY (nil = chosen but not instantiated), +0x20 f32 threshold compared against two constants, +0x48 ptr whose +0x2fc is read. R.poi.placed() returns {name=, entity=} per tile. NOTE ON SCOPE: this closes PLACEMENT only. A mod POI still has two unbuilt gates, both entity COMPONENTS and therefore both blocked by the same wall (a level cannot reference a mod-owned entity, and an in-place override cannot ADD a component): a minimap marker (oCDtEntityCpntMinimapMarkerSettings) and an interaction. The only route is `swaps` -- stand a SHIPPED entity that already carries them at one of the tile's own transforms. Corpus check 2026-09-04: Reward_Spawner_Interactive_Model carries both but is NOT placeable (a sub-entity a spawner selects; _validated_swaps refuses it, and swapping to one builds nothing and crashes). The placeable parents ARE legal targets -- Enemy_Camp_Reward_Spawner_<biome>, Map_Boss_Spawner_<biome>, <biome>_Key_Keeper -- so the chest spawner is the test, and it exercises both gates at once. PER-TIER SLOT COUNTS located 2026-09-04: the driver picks between THREE ints by comparing the kind's tier float (entry+0x20) against two constants — `movss xmm0,[r12+0x20]` then `[r13+0x2fc]` (T1) / `[r13+0x300]` (T2) / `[r13+0x304]` (T3) at 0x140344748..0x140344777. That is the numeric half of the documented rule that a tiledef's `weight` is a TIER field (T1 0.0 / T2 0.33 / T3 0.667), not a spawn rate. r13 is live across basic blocks and awkward to trace statically, but FUN_1403429d0 reaches the SAME three fields via the placement element — `mov rcx,[r12+0x48]` then `mov r8d,[rcx+0x2fc]` — so element+0x48 is the owner and R.poi.placed() now reads it, RTTI-naming the class rather than inferring it. Entries carry slots={t1,t2,t3} and slots_class. OWNER PINNED IN-GAME 2026-09-04 (session 674f): element+0x48 is an **oCDtTileDefinition** — RTTI-named at runtime, so the placement record points straight at the tiledef, which is a cleaner identity than the settings-resource name at payload+0xa0. ⚠ BUT the three ints read 0/0/0 on a mod tile, so +0x2fc/+0x300/+0x304 are NOT confirmed as the per-tier counts on this object: a single all-zero sample cannot separate 'wrong offsets' from 'this tile genuinely carries zeros', and those are opposite conclusions. Reading them across all 141 placed tiles is the discriminator and is instrumented. Do not treat the tier counts as located until a vanilla tile reads non-zero. ✗ CORRECTION 2026-09-04 (session 794f): the shortcut was WRONG and the per-tier SLOT COUNTS are NOT located. Reading +0x2fc/+0x300/+0x304 across all 140 placed tiles: 138 read 0/0/0, only 2 are non-zero, and one of those is 40x40_DarkHills_Thieves_Stashes_Entrance_Cursed_Room_01 = 2/3/4. So the offsets ARE meaningful fields on an oCDtTileDefinition (2/3/4 is a plausible tier triple) but a field that only 2 of 140 tiles populate cannot be the per-KIND slot count the driver reads. FUN_1403429d0's `[element+0x48]+0x2fc` and the driver's `[r13]+0x2fc` are DIFFERENT OBJECTS that happen to share an offset — assuming they were the same is what produced the bad reading. r13 is still unpinned; tracing it needs real control-flow work across basic blocks, not a shortcut. symbols.name: LevelStream_Deserialize
symbols.signature: bool(void* loader, void* a_pLevel, void* a_pLvlId, void* a_pLinks)
symbols.note: [2026-09-12] The body shared by LevelBinary_Load and LevelText_Load, and the top of the level's stream grammar. Register signature: rcx = loader (constructed on LevelBinary_Load's stack by FUN_140500160, most-derived vftable 0x140f4a690), rdx = a_pLevel (the container, LevelStream_LoadStep's level+0x10), r8 = a_pLvlId, r9 = a_pLinks. It writes a u32 version = 1 and then THREE bools (`a_pLvlId != 0`, `a_pLinks != 0`, `a_pLevel != 0`) through the loader's bool slot, and only then reads the three objects, EACH through its own full Serializer_ReadObjectNamed call: `*a_pLvlId`, `*a_pLinks`, `*a_pLevel`, in that order, with `oDummyLvlId` / `oDummyLinks` substituted when the caller passes null. ⚠ THREE INDEPENDENT OBJECT GRAPHS, not one. Each of the three carries its OWN class table and its OWN object table, so a level file contains three `uOjbectsCount` fields and only the LAST one (the `*a_pLevel` graph) is the level's. That is why the 7 bytes `01 00 00 00 01 01 01` sit between the cooked header and the first MARK_BEGIN, and why rsmm.engine.cooked.parse cannot read a level's inner stream directly — it expects the marker there.

symbols.name: Serializer_ReadObjectNamed
symbols.signature: bool(void* loader, void* root, const char* name)
symbols.note:
[2026-09-12] Slot +0x28 of the loader vftable, and THE WRITER OF THE CONTAINER'S OBJECT VECTOR — found by reading the write side from LevelStream_Deserialize's `*a_pLevel` call rather than by guessing where to read it. Reads one whole object graph, in four phases, all sequential (there is no seek and no index anywhere in the file):

  1. CLASS TABLE. MARK_BEGIN, `uClassCount` (rejected above 0x200), then per class {`rInfo.m_sName` lstr, `rInfo.m_uId`, `rInfo.m_uVersionMaj`, `rInfo.m_uVersionMin`, `rInfo.m_uParentId`}, then MARK_END. Kept at ctx+0x6d0 (data) / ctx+0x6d8 (count), where ctx = loader[+0x18]. This is exactly the table rsmm.engine.cooked.parse already decodes.
  2. OBJECT TABLE. MARK_BEGIN, `uOjbectsCount` (the engine's own typo — grep for Ojbect, not Object), then ONE `uClassFinfoIndex` per object indexing the class table, then MARK_END. For each entry it looks the metaclass id up in the global class registry at 0x14143ccd0, type-checks it, INSTANTIATES it through the descriptor's vftable +0x88, and push_backs the instance into the vector at ctx+0x6e0 (data) / ctx+0x6e8 (size). **This phase is what decides how many objects exist and what they are.** It also sets loader[+0x8] = root.
  3. PAYLOADS. For i in 0..count-1, Serializer_ReadObjectPayload(loader, objectTable[i], "") — strictly in table order, strictly sequential in the stream, with no cross-check that the block it lands on is the class the table promised.
  4. ROOT. The same call once more for the object and name the caller passed (`*a_pLevel`), AFTER every sub-object exists. That is why the container's own poly-pointer vector is at the END of the stream and why `level_placements._object_vector`'s "last MARK_BEGIN" heuristic lands on the right bytes.

CORPUS PROOF, 390/390 shipped levels (data/uncooked/Ot/**/*.level.ot.GameStream.gen), three independent invariants: the `*a_pLevel` graph's object table of count m is followed by exactly m payload blocks plus one root block; `objectTable[i]` equals the leading class index of payload block i, so **an object's id IS its position in the stream**; and the root's leading poly-ptr vector is always an identity prefix 0..k-1 with k <= m (equal in 113 levels, strictly less in 277 — Map_Avalon_Terrain is 12370 objects under a root vector of 1, the rest being children of that one terrain object).

WHAT THIS FIXED, 2026-09-12. `rsmm.engine.level_placements` was written against the bytes BETWEEN a level's asset references, and that space does not line up with the object graph. Two consequences, both measured and both now gone. (1) `add_placement` grew only the root's poly-pointer vector, never `uOjbectsCount` and never a `uClassFinfoIndex` — so on four shipped levels the output had one more payload block than the engine would read, which does not orphan the new object but shifts every following one onto its predecessor's bytes and leaves the root's own block to be consumed as the last sub-object. (2) `decode()` paired each entity reference with the bytes that FOLLOW it, but a reference sits near the end of its own block, so every placement in every level was reported with its SUCCESSOR's position and rotation and the last one with a run of zeros — the oracle the POI work used to judge whether a prop stands upright was reading the neighbouring prop. Rewritten on this grammar the decoder reads 350 levels and 116708 placements where the old walk read 280 and 7686.

symbols.name: Serializer_ReadObjectPayload
symbols.signature: bool(void* loader, void* obj, const char* name)
symbols.note:
[2026-09-12] Slot +0xa0 of the loader vftable: read ONE object's payload block. MARK_BEGIN (a raw u32 compared against 0xaabb1111), then `uClassInfoIndex` bound-checked against the class table count at ctx+0x6d8, then dispatch into that class's Serialize via FUN_1404fe970 with the object it was handed. ⚠ IT NEVER RECONCILES THE INDEX IT READS WITH THE CLASS THE OBJECT TABLE PROMISED FOR THIS SLOT. Since Serializer_ReadObjectNamed calls this once per object in table order with no seek, inserting one payload block into a stream without growing `uOjbectsCount` does not orphan the new object — it shifts every following object onto its predecessor's bytes and deserializes them into an instance of the wrong class, and the root's own block is then read as the last sub-object. The failure is a corrupt graph, not a missing one.

PLACEMENT BLOCK LAYOUT, mined for `level_placements` (corpus, 2026-09-12): `u32 uClassInfoIndex`, `lstr` instance name, `lstr` group name, 0x26 bytes of flags and defaults, then the transform (`float3` position, `float4` quaternion, `float3` scale), then later the literal `lstr "EntitySettings"` followed by the `lstr` path of the entity placed. That makes the transform's offset STRUCTURAL rather than searched: it resolves 116708 of 116708 marker-free placement blocks. ⚠ A block that frames a nested MARK_BEGIN is where a spawner keeps the poly-pointer vector of the settings objects it OWNS, so copying one hands a second spawner the same children; 164687 marker-free blocks own nothing, and no level with owned children lacks a marker-bearing block. 2996 groups of shipped blocks are byte-identical apart from transform and reference, so a placement carries no per-object identity to remint.

symbols.name: Serializer_ResolveObjectId
symbols.signature: bool(void* loader, void** out, const char* label)
symbols.note: [2026-09-12] Slot +0xa8 of the loader vftable — the "poly resolve" Serializer_ReadPolyPtrVector's note refers to, now read rather than inferred. Reads a u32 `uOjbectId` and turns it into a pointer: 0xffffffff = NULL, 0xfffffffe = the ROOT object (loader[+0x8], stashed by Serializer_ReadObjectNamed), anything else = objectTable[id] out of the vector at ctx+0x6e0. **This is the whole meaning of an id in a cooked file: an index into the object table that phase 2 built, hence an index into stream position.** The bound check is `id > size -> fail`, so `id == size` is let through and reads one slot past the used region — an off-by-one worth knowing before trusting an appended id.

symbols.name: Chapter_Serialize
symbols.note:
GameModeDefInternal::Chapter — vftable 0x140ed7968 slot 3, and the most important find for a NET-NEW CHAPTER. Layout: u8 @+0x08, u8 @+0x09, then a DISCRIMINATED UNION on +0x09 — nonzero reads a resref @+0x10 through ResourceRef_Serialize, zero reads a plain u32 enum @+0x0c through Serializer_ReadEnum. NEITHER BRANCH IS VERSION-GATED.

All four shipped chapters in All_Chapters.gamemodedefaultdef take the ENUM branch (+0x09 = 0, +0x0c = 0,1,2,3 and +0x08 = 1,1,1,0 — false on the last, so it reads as 'a chapter follows'). The enum is what binds a chapter to one of the four built-in biome map ids registered by the blackboard registrar, and it is why 'add a fifth chapter' has always looked blocked.

The resref branch is the way out, and it is LIVE CODE, not a hypothesis: GameModeDefaultDef_PostLoad walks the chapter vector at +0x290/+0x298 and for every chapter with +0x09 != 0 calls ResourceRef_Resolve on +0x10 unless it is already resolved. So a chapter can name its content by asset path instead of by index, the engine resolves it at load, and nothing in that path is gated on a version or a flag. ⚠ WHAT THE REF POINTS AT IS NOT PROVEN — the expected class is held in a runtime-initialised global, so it cannot be read statically. A mapdef is the hypothesis (the tile-generation level carries a mapdef resref of exactly this shape) and it needs a playtest, not more static reading.

symbols.name: GameModifierUi_PadSelectedSlots
symbols.signature: void(void* uiController, void* unknown, void* selectedVector)
symbols.note:
Pads the SELECTED game-modifier list out to five entries for display. rcx = the GameModifierUi controller (its settings at [rcx+0x10], m_bDisplayEmptySlots at settings+0xf8 gates the whole thing), r8 = a {void* data; u32 count} vector. Body at 0x140360c58: `cmp [r8+8], 5; jae out` then a loop appending a null entry while `[rbx+8] < 5`.

WHY IT MATTERS, and the correction it carries: this five is a FLOOR, not a ceiling. It only ever APPENDS, never trims, so a selected list already holding six would render six. The long-standing '5 negative modes' cap was assumed to live here (and, before that, in the challenge-page asset's slot widgets -- the page has none: the list is spawner-driven). A sweep of all 77 functions in the challenge-page controller cluster and all 91 in this one found NO `count >= 5` bound anywhere; every other small compare is a boolean test. So the refusal that fires `Modifier Added Fail FMod Event` is most likely 'no free slot among five positions' rather than a numeric limit, and the sibling at 0x140360720 has the shape of that slot search.

Hooked read-only to answer the one question static reading cannot: what count actually ARRIVES here. If it tops out at five the ceiling is upstream in the add path; if it can exceed five, the display already scales and only that slot search needs lifting. Six callers, all display-refresh paths (0x14034d900, 0x14035c9c0, 0x1403e8f80, 0x140426ab0, 0x140426d60, 0x1404293f0). Backs R.modifier.on_slots.

⚠ Raising the cap is NOT just this constant: the selected set is seeded run state under a deterministic-shared multiplayer scope, so every peer must agree or the run desyncs.

symbols.name: Vector_InsertRange
symbols.signature: void*(void* vector, unsigned index, unsigned count)
symbols.note:
Inserts `count` uninitialised elements into a {void* data; u32 count; u32 capacity} vector at `index`, growing the allocation when count+n exceeds capacity, and RETURNS a pointer to the first inserted element -- so the caller writes the payload itself. Read off the prologue: esi = [rcx+8] (count), eax = [rcx+0xc] (capacity), ebp = edx (index), r14d = r8d (n), then `lea ebx,[rsi+r14]; cmp eax,ebx; jae` skips the realloc.

NOT `Vector_Grow` (0x140155230), which is a different function -- do not conflate them. 286 call sites across the engine, so this is the generic sequence-insert, not something specific to one system.

WHY IT IS NAMED: `GameModifierUi_PadSelectedSlots` calls it in a loop to pad the selected-modifier list out to five empty slots (`mov r8d,1; mov edx,[rbx+8]; call; mov [rax],0`), and the modifier UI draws ONE WIDGET PER VECTOR ELEMENT. So appending through this helper is how the SDK can offer a sixth slot without patching a single byte -- the experiment that decides whether the 5-modifier cap is the slot list or a bound in the store.

⚠ WRITE path into live engine state. Every use must validate the vector first (R.ptr.vector_valid) and stay on the thread that owns it; a bad `index` writes past the end of a real allocation.

These are confirmed names harvested by string-xref (cluster 0x140f13a00-0x140f13f00); subscribe via R.on('<name>', cb) with RSMM_ENABLE_GAME_EVENTS=1. Shown by `rsmm symbols events`.

Subscribe with R.on('gameplay:<NAME>', cb). event_payload_schemas_doc:
Payload layouts for the oCGameNamedEvent subclasses that carry data, recovered by tools/mine_event_payloads.py (RTTI type descriptor -> complete object locator -> vftable -> the code that stores it, walked within .pdata function bounds). Keyed by VFTABLE RVA, not event name: the loader reads *(ev+0) and matches it exactly, so no name mapping can go wrong. Field OFFSETS and WIDTHS are recovered; field MEANING is not, so names are mechanical (u50 = u32 at +0x50) except where hand-RE confirmed one. Only ~24 of the ~150 event names have a payload at all -- the rest are dispatched as the bare base class (header only). RVAs are build-specific: the loader gates this decode on the build fingerprint (va_globals_trusted) and re-verifies with --verify after a patch.

RULED OUT 2026-09-11, so the next reader does not re-run the miner to find out: there is NO skill or talent payload class. A re-mine of the shipped exe finds 3274 RTTI classes with a vftable and exactly 26 event payload classes, none of them skill-related, so UPGRADE_LOWER_SKILL, UPGRADE_SPECIFIC_SKILL, UPGRADE_RANDOM_SKILL and UPGRADE_LOWER_SKILL_TO_LEGENDARY are all dispatched as the bare base class: a subscriber learns that a talent was upgraded and cannot learn WHICH. That is a property of the engine, not a gap in the mining. Anything needing talent identity (a 'build around your POWER ability' rule, a talent-pick counter) therefore cannot be built on the event bus at all and needs the hero's skill state read or the upgrade routine hooked for its arguments -- and note that no skill/talent function is named in this map or in Ghidra yet, so that is a cold RE session, not a lookup. ⚠ CORRECTED the same day: that conclusion covers the GAMEPLAY bus only. The ANALYTICS bus does carry skill identity — see Analytics_EmitSkillSelected, which submits skill_name, skill_tier and skill_rarity. Do not read the paragraph above as 'talent identity is unobtainable'.
